# How long does it take to hire a CMO, CFO or CHRO?
URL: https://boardroomcxo.com/executive-search-faq/time-to-hire-cmo-cfo-chro
Published: 2026-11-04
Publisher: Boardroom CXO (https://boardroomcxo.com)
Reviewed by: CA Ketul Patel, Founder, Boardroom CXO (https://www.linkedin.com/in/caketul/)
================================================================================

With Boardroom CXO, a CMO or CHRO search typically takes 30 to 45 days to an offer. In that time we map what the role pays in your category and city, agree the brief, approach and shortlist people already doing the job, and take you to an offer. The start date then depends on the leader's notice period.

## The timeline, stage by stage

- Pay map: we map what the role pays across your category and city.
- Role brief: we agree the outcomes, authority and KPIs for the next 12 to 24 months.
- Search: we approach people already doing the job at competitor companies and build a confidential shortlist.
- Offer stage: interviews, the offer and acceptance, with a realistic uplift of usually 25 to 30%.

For a CMO or CHRO, these stages typically take 30 to 45 days from the start of the search to an offer.

## What our case studies show

For a pre-IPO jewellery brand whose earlier CFO searches had stalled for months, we shortlisted four CFOs from listed retail companies, and the time to placement was 8 weeks. For a Singapore company entering India, a Finance Head was placed in 6 weeks. Every search is different, and both are on our case studies page.

## What changes between a CMO, CFO and CHRO search

The stages are the same. What changes is the profile we screen for. A CMO search for a retail or D2C brand needs the right mix of brand building and ROAS-literate performance marketing. A CFO search often needs pre-IPO, SEBI or cross-border experience. A CHRO search for a brand adding stores needs someone who can scale hiring and culture across a growing network. The narrower the profile, the smaller the pool of people to approach.

## What adds time after the offer

The biggest variable after acceptance is the notice period. A sitting CXO has to serve the notice period in their current contract before they can join. Ask about the notice period at the first conversation with each shortlisted candidate, so the start date is planned, not a surprise.

## How to keep a search moving

Searches slow down when the budget is still open, when the interview panel is not agreed, or when feedback on candidates takes weeks. Agree the budget after the pay map, name the panel at the start, and give feedback within a few days of each interview.


================================================================================
# What is the difference between retained and contingency search?
URL: https://boardroomcxo.com/executive-search-faq/retained-vs-contingency-search
Published: 2026-11-04
Publisher: Boardroom CXO (https://boardroomcxo.com)
Reviewed by: CA Ketul Patel, Founder, Boardroom CXO (https://www.linkedin.com/in/caketul/)
================================================================================

In retained search, a company pays a search firm a fee at the start and the firm works the role exclusively, usually for senior roles. In contingency recruitment, an agency is paid only when its candidate is hired, and several agencies can work the same role. Boardroom CXO charges Rs 10,000 (including GST) at the start and the rest on joining, and does not ask for exclusivity.

## Retained search

The Association of Executive Search and Leadership Consultants (AESC), the global body for the profession, describes retained executive search as focused on executive and senior-level positions and board directors. A consulting fee or retainer is charged at the beginning of the relationship, and retained firms work on an exclusive basis.

## Contingency recruitment

The AESC describes contingency recruiters as agencies paid after a candidate has been identified and hired. A company is not tied to one agency and may use several on the same role. Contingency recruiters typically fill entry-level to mid-level positions.

## Where Boardroom CXO sits

We start each search with a Rs 10,000 service fee (including GST), which is not refundable. It is adjusted against the final fee of one month's CTC, which is invoiced when your hire joins. Most of the fee is therefore tied to a hire, while the search itself works the way executive search does: we map pay, define the role, and headhunt directly from competitor companies rather than sending CVs from a database.

Unlike a retained search, our searches are not exclusive: you are free to use other agencies on the same role. If the hire leaves within 90 days, we find one replacement free.

## Which model fits which hire

For a high-volume or junior role, where many qualified people are actively applying, a contingency agency or a job portal can be enough. For a CXO role, the best candidate is usually already doing the job somewhere else and is not looking. Reaching them takes research and a confidential approach, which is the work a search firm is paid to do.

## Questions to ask any firm before you sign

- What do I pay before a hire is made, and what do I pay when the hire joins?
- Is the firm working the role alone, or alongside other agencies?
- Will candidates come from a database of applicants, or from a direct approach to people in role?
- How is the client's name kept confidential during the approach?
- What happens if the hire leaves early? Ask for it in writing.

## Sources

- AESC, Retained Executive Search vs Contingency: What's the Difference?, https://www.aesc.org/insights/blog/retained-executive-search-vs-contingency-whats-difference, accessed November 2026


================================================================================
# Executive search firm vs recruitment agency vs job portal: what is the difference?
URL: https://boardroomcxo.com/executive-search-faq/executive-search-vs-recruitment-agency
Published: 2026-11-04
Publisher: Boardroom CXO (https://boardroomcxo.com)
Reviewed by: CA Ketul Patel, Founder, Boardroom CXO (https://www.linkedin.com/in/caketul/)
================================================================================

A job portal lists your opening and waits for people to apply. A generalist recruitment agency usually sends CVs of people who are already looking. An executive search firm researches the market and confidentially approaches leaders who are not job-hunting, often at competitors. For a CXO role, the best candidate is usually in that last group.

## Job portals: reach people who are looking

A job portal is a listing. You post the role, and the people who see it and are open to a move apply. That works well when many qualified people are actively searching, such as frontline or store roles. It does not reach the leader who is busy running a function and is not reading job listings.

## Generalist recruitment agencies

A generalist agency fills roles across many functions and levels, often from applicants and job-board databases. It can be quick for roles with a large pool of active candidates. For a senior role, the risk is a stack of CVs from people who are available, not a shortlist of the people best suited to the job.

## Executive search firms

An executive search firm starts from the market, not from applicants. At Boardroom CXO we map what the role pays across your category and city, agree what the role must deliver, and then approach people already doing the job at competitor companies. Candidates choose to go further before your name is disclosed, and you see a confidential shortlist.

## Why it matters for CXO roles

The strongest CMOs, CFOs, CHROs and sales heads in a category are not applying anywhere. A CMO who can build brand equity and a performance marketer who is genuinely ROAS-literate are different skill sets, and people with both are already inside a competitor's growth team. The CFOs who have taken a company through an IPO are already CFOs somewhere. Reaching them takes research, timing and a confidential approach, not a job posting.

## Which one to use

- Job portal: high-volume roles with many active applicants.
- Recruitment agency: mid-level roles where speed matters more than reaching people who are not looking.
- Executive search: CXO and senior leadership roles, confidential replacements, and roles where the right person is at a competitor.


================================================================================
# How does a confidential executive search work?
URL: https://boardroomcxo.com/executive-search-faq/confidential-executive-search
Published: 2026-11-04
Publisher: Boardroom CXO (https://boardroomcxo.com)
Reviewed by: CA Ketul Patel, Founder, Boardroom CXO (https://www.linkedin.com/in/caketul/)
================================================================================

In a confidential executive search, the search firm approaches candidates without naming your company. Candidates first hear what the role involves, and only those who choose to go further learn who the client is. There is no public job advert, so your team, your competitors and the market do not learn that you are hiring.

## Why companies run a search quietly

Many senior hires cannot be announced while the search is on. A company may be replacing a leader who is still in the role, building a function it has not announced, preparing for an IPO, or entering a new market. A public advert for any of these tells employees, competitors and investors more than the company wants them to know.

## How the approach works

At Boardroom CXO the approach is intermediary-led. We research who is already doing the job at competitor companies and approach them on your behalf. The first conversation is about the role, the scope and what it must deliver. Candidates self-select in before your name is disclosed, so only serious candidates ever learn who the client is.

## What you see, and when

You see the market first: what the role pays across your category and city. Then you see a confidential shortlist of people who have already said they are interested. Interviews start only at that point, so your senior team's time goes to candidates who are genuinely in play.

## Discretion protects candidates too

The people approached for a CXO role are usually in senior jobs already. They are taking a risk by talking to anyone about a move, and a careless approach can reach their current employer. A confidential process lets them explore the role without that risk, which is one reason strong candidates respond to a search firm and not to a job post.

## What we publish about clients

Our case studies describe the role and the outcome, such as a CFO for a pre-IPO jewellery brand, without naming the company, and on our UAE page the client identity is kept confidential.

## Starting a confidential search

You can brief us on a free 30-minute call, by WhatsApp or by email. Tell us the role, the city and any constraints on who may know about the search, and we will plan the approach around them.

# How do you hire a CXO for a UAE company?

Publisher: Boardroom CXO (https://boardroomcxo.com)
Reviewed by: CA Ketul Patel, Founder, Boardroom CXO (https://www.linkedin.com/in/caketul/)
================================================================================

To hire a CXO for a UAE company, first decide whether the leader should be a local UAE hire or sourced from India or elsewhere, then check what the role pays and approach people already doing it. Boardroom CXO runs searches for companies in Dubai and across the UAE, including India-based brands building a Gulf team.

## Local hire or India-sourced?

We look at leaders already working in the UAE first. International sourcing, from India, the Philippines, Europe, the US or the UK, is available when a client specifically wants it, for example when the role needs experience the local pool does not have.

## India-based brands building a Gulf team

For an India-based brand building a Gulf team, the question is often whether to move a trusted leader from India, hire locally, or do both: a local head with an India-sourced second line. We map both options before you decide.

## Map the pay before you set the budget

Pay varies by seniority and scope, and a generic salary survey is a weak guide. We map what the role pays in the market before you commit a budget, so the offer is neither too low to close nor higher than it needs to be.

## Roles we search for in the UAE

Senior and CXO roles only: CEOs, MDs and business heads, CFOs and finance heads, CMOs and marketing heads, sales and business development heads, and CHROs. We run them for companies in Dubai and across the UAE, including consulting, business-setup and corporate service firms. See our UAE search page.

## What a UAE search costs

AED 1,000 starts the search. It is adjusted against the final fee of one month's salary, invoiced when your hire joins.

## How the search runs

The method is the same as in India. We map what the role pays, agree what it must deliver over the next 12 to 24 months, approach people already doing the job at competitor companies, and give you a confidential shortlist and a realistic offer number. Our first consultation is free.

## How to start

Call or WhatsApp +91 98567 55000, which covers India and the UAE, or email hire@boardroomcxo.com with the role and the city. It helps to say at the start whether the leader must already be based in the UAE, and who inside the company may know about the search.

# What is CXO hiring?
URL: https://boardroomcxo.com/executive-search-faq/what-is-cxo-hiring
Published: 2026-11-04
Publisher: Boardroom CXO (https://boardroomcxo.com)
Reviewed by: CA Ketul Patel, Founder, Boardroom CXO (https://www.linkedin.com/in/caketul/)
================================================================================

CXO hiring means recruiting for a company's top roles, the chief officers whose titles take the form "Chief X Officer", such as the CEO, CFO, CMO and CHRO, along with the leaders just below them. Because the best candidates for these roles are rarely job-hunting, CXO hiring is usually done through executive search rather than job adverts.

## Which roles count as CXO

The "X" stands for the function. The roles we search for include the CEO, MD and business heads; the CFO and finance heads; the CMO and Chief Growth Officer; chief sales officers and national sales heads; and the CHRO. Every search we run is for a role that reports to the board, the founder or the CEO, or to someone who does.

## Why CXO hiring is different

A CXO hire shapes the business for years, and the pool of people who have done the job at the right scale is small. Those people are already running a function for someone else. They do not apply to adverts, and they expect a confidential, well-researched approach before they will consider a move. A wrong CXO hire is also hard to undo, so the brief, the pay benchmark and the offer matter as much as finding names.

## How a CXO hire usually runs

With Boardroom CXO, a search starts with a map of what the role pays across your category and city, then an agreed brief on what the role must deliver over the next 12 to 24 months. We then approach people already doing the job at competitor companies and build a confidential shortlist, and at the offer stage we give you a realistic uplift, usually 25 to 30%. See how executive search works for each stage.

## CXO hiring with Boardroom CXO

We run CXO searches for companies in India and the UAE across five sectors: retail and jewellery, where our network is deepest; consumer and D2C; financial services, including banks, NBFCs, insurers and wealth firms; manufacturing; and technology and IT services.

## What it costs

A Rs 10,000 service fee (including GST) starts the search. It is not refundable, and it is adjusted against the final fee of one month's CTC, invoiced when your hire joins. The first consultation is free. For a worked example, see how much a CXO search costs in India.

# Leadership hiring and moves in India 2026
URL: https://boardroomcxo.com/leadership-moves-india-statistics-2026
Published: 2026-11-04
Publisher: Boardroom CXO (https://boardroomcxo.com)
================================================================================

Boardroom Moves announced 79 senior leadership moves in India between 6 December 2025 and 30 October 2026. 63 of the 79 leaders (80%) joined from another organisation and 15 (19%) were promoted inside their company or group. These counts cover the announcements Boardroom CXO tracked on its LinkedIn page, not every leadership move in India. Function and sector groups are read from the job title, the company's business and what the announcement says the role does.

## Moves by function

- Sales and business development: 13 (16%)
- Business head (CBO, business unit or P&L head): 12 (15%)
- HR and talent (including CHRO): 12 (15%)
- CEO, MD and country head: 8 (10%)
- Operations (including COO): 7 (9%)
- Marketing, brand and content (including CMO): 5 (6%)
- Supply chain and procurement: 5 (6%)
- Technology, data and product: 5 (6%)
- Consulting and advisory practice: 4 (5%)
- Finance, investment and credit (including CFO): 3 (4%)
- Other (strategy, advisory, innovation): 3 (4%)
- Legal and company secretarial: 2 (3%)

## Chief-level titles (21 of 79)

- Chief Business Officer (CBO): 6
- Chief Operating Officer (COO): 4
- Chief Executive Officer (CEO): 2
- Deputy CEO: 1
- Chief Financial Officer (CFO): 1
- Chief Marketing Officer (CMO): 1
- Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO): 1
- Chief Sales Officer (CSO): 1
- Other chief titles: 4
- No Chief Technology Officer move was announced in this period.

## Moves by sector

- Technology and IT services: 18 (23%)
- Banking, financial services and insurance: 8 (10%)
- Industrial, manufacturing, auto and building materials: 8 (10%)
- Energy, power and infrastructure: 7 (9%)
- Media, advertising, entertainment and sport: 7 (9%)
- Consulting, audit and staffing: 5 (6%)
- FMCG, food and agri: 5 (6%)
- Healthcare and pharma: 5 (6%)
- Real estate: 5 (6%)
- E-commerce and internet platforms: 4 (5%)
- Education, research and public bodies: 4 (5%)
- Hospitality, travel and food service: 2 (3%)
- Diversified group: 1 (1%)

## Promoted inside or hired from outside

- Joined from another organisation: 63 (80%)
- Promoted or moved up inside the same company or group: 15 (19%)
- Not stated in the announcement: 1 (1%)
- 3 of the outside hires returned to a former employer.

## Moves by month

- December 2025: 12
- January 2026: 8
- February 2026: 8
- March 2026: 3
- April 2026: 0
- May 2026: 4
- June 2026: 6
- July 2026: 5
- August 2026: 10
- September 2026: 10
- October 2026: 13

Monthly totals follow how often the page posted, not the market.

## Cities

74 of the 79 announcements name no city. Where one is named: Pune (2), Delhi (1), Hyderabad (1), Indore (1).

## October 2026 monthly report

The Boardroom Moves desk tracked 36 senior leadership moves announced between 17 October and 27 October 2026 (https://boardroomcxo.com/moves/report/2026-10). Marketing and brand roles moved most (13) and technology and IT services had the most appointments (9). The report uses its own groups and overlaps with the moves above.

## The wider market

Naukri JobSpeak for October 2026 (Info Edge), which measures new white-collar job postings on Naukri.com, reported 14% year-on-year growth in white-collar hiring, 22% growth in hiring for professionals with more than 16 years of experience, led by auto and FMCG, and 21% growth in gems and jewellery hiring. These are job postings, not appointments.

## Data

CSV of every move: https://boardroomcxo.com/leadership-moves-india-statistics-2026.csv
